elements.texte:
[cheerful] To keep every change, the sales team added the price underscore history table.

It keeps the product involved, the old price, the new price and the date of the change.

For now, no change is recorded in it.

A TRIGGER is a block of SQL code that runs automatically when an event happens.

For example: adding, changing or deleting data.

Here, every time a product’s price changes, the trigger records the old price, the new one and the date.

It adds them to the price underscore history table.

You don’t have to add this row to the history yourself.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] CREATE TRIGGER creates the trigger, here named track underscore price.

AFTER UPDATE ON products means “after a change in the products table”.

It sets when the trigger steps in.

When sets the condition to meet: the old price (old dot price) must be different from the new one (new dot price).

If the price stays the same, nothing is added to the history.

BEGIN and end wrap the instructions to run automatically.

Here, insert into adds a row to the price underscore history table.

It holds the product’s identifier, the old price, the new price and the date of the change.

Old dot price gives the old price, new dot price the new one.

Current timestamp gives the date and time of the change.

Your turn!

Click the “Create the trigger” button.

The trigger is now attached to the products table.
